rule.text: Fishkeeping World: 2-3 fish in 10 gal, add 5 gal per extra fish; Aquarium Source table 3 fish at 10 gal, +5 gal each (counts fish, not males)

points.quote: Two or three gouramis can be easily kept in a 10-gallon tank.
For each additional fish make sure to add 5 gallons.
Keep at least a couple of females for every male.
add an additional 5 gallons for each new fish
just about big enough for a pair
It's generally not a good idea to keep a group of dwarf gouramis together.
one as a centerpiece fish with other community tank mates

notes: AMBIGUOUS: Fishkeeping World and Aquarium Source scale fish count by volume (no male limit); Seriously Fish and Aquarium Co-Op say one male or one pair only and warn against groups. The volume rule is a fish-count rule; male territory is not quantified. Seriously Fish 56 L = about 14 gal.

points.quote: sufficient for a single pair
command a territory a couple of feet across when breeding

notes: Only one pair per 24x12 in, territory about 2 ft across when breeding (inference: +1 pair per about 24 in length, not stated). No per-additional-pair rule found. Quotes are fragments the fetch tool returned in quotation marks. Use existing expert-curve points for counts.

rule.text: Furry Critter: adding ten to fifteen gallons per additional pair, from a 20 gal first pair (retailer site, single source)

points.quote: adding ten to fifteen gallons per additional pair is a reasonable guideline
Start with a minimum tank size of 20 gallons.
For more than one kribensis cichlid, start with a 30-gallon tank.
A 10-gallon (38-liter) aquarium is large enough for a single pair.
it is even possible to house several couples in the same tank
no less than 90cm/36" long
A single pair does well in a 60-litre tank.

notes: Spawning territory radius about 20-30 cm (Gensou, paraphrased). Per-pair increment rests on one retailer source; first-pair size varies 10 gal (TFH), 16 (Gensou), 20 (FW, Furry Critter). TFH says several couples are possible with caves.

points.quote: One male for every two to three females is a good ratio.
would do best in a 20-gallon aquarium or larger
60 x 30 cm (24 x 12 in) or more, acceptable for a single pair

notes: Seriously Fish quote is a paraphrase by the fetch tool. One male with 2-3 females per 20 gal is the only stated unit; no scaling rule found (female territory about 30 cm radius appears only on Wikipedia and forums, not used). Aquarium Co-Op says a 10 gal works for breeding.

points.quote: This territorial behavior is primarily due to breeding.
having just one as the centerpiece fish in your aquarium seems to make them much more easygoing and docile overall
Keep silver angelfish in a school of six or more.
a group of six juvenile fish

notes: Basis volume with height (needs 20 in tall). No stated rule beyond points already in expert-curve.json (29 gal/4, 55 gal/5-6, 75 gal/4). Seriously Fish quote is a fetch-tool paraphrase; the six are juveniles to pair off. Fishkeeping World gives no per-gallon rule.

rule.text: Males: one per tank, never two in open water. Female sorority: four to six in a 20-gal long; above six conflicts rise. Not scaled further.

points.quote: four to six female bettas sharing a heavily planted 20-gallon
Above six, tank volume and territory conflicts rise faster than the social benefit.
A sorority is made up of four to six female bettas, preferably all of the same age.
If you plan to keep a sorority, you'll need at least a 20-gallon tank.
Never open-water two males regardless of volume.
only a single individual can be kept per tank in most cases

notes: Males: 1 per tank at any size (unit fish). Sorority: group-size rule (minimum 4, about 6 in a 20 gal long); the unit is the group, not a territory. A 10 gal sorority is not supported by good sources. Tankarium points already in expert-curve.

rule.text: Fishkeeping World: at least a 20-gallon tank for up to 5; For each additional Tiger Barb added, make sure to add 3 gallons

points.quote: Tiger Barbs need at least a 20-gallon tank - this would be suitable for up to 5 of them.
So 8 Tiger Barbs would need at least a 29-gallon tank.
For each additional Tiger Barb added, make sure to add 3 gallons.

notes: Stated rule, but a space rule, not a territory rule: nipping is tied to group size (min 5-8, no more than 12 per the same page), so the cap is really a school floor and ceiling. Same page as the existing expert-curve points.

rule.text: Fishkeeping World: minimum tank size 10 gallons, add 2 gallons per extra fish (fetch-tool paraphrase)

points.quote: Zebra danios are schooling fish that should be kept in groups of at least five.
Minimum tank size: 10 gallons

notes: Danio is a school floor, not a territory fish; too few stresses them, too many cause hyperactivity and territorial behavior (paraphrase). The +2 gal per fish is paraphrased by the fetch tool, not verbatim. Nipping is aimed at other species, so a territory cap is likely not needed. Gensou 16 gal/6 already in expert-curve.

rule.text: Fishkeeping World: minimum 15 gal for one swordtail, increase size by 5 gallons per additional fish; 1:3 male to female

points.quote: Increase size by 5 gallons per additional fish.
1:3 male to female ratio
Females must outweigh the number of males in the tank. Otherwise, swordtail males become territorial and aggressive.
the ideal is probably a single male alongside five females
Males can be extremely aggressive towards each other.

notes: Territory is controlled by sex ratio (1 male : 3-5 females), not size; no stated cap on males per volume. The Fishkeeping World volume rule is a fish count (paraphrased quote); implied 30 gal = 4 fish = 1M+3F. PFK tank 90x38x38 cm is about 36 gal.

rule.text: One male per 48x18 in tank with 3-6 females; more males only in 100+ gal. No per-male increment stated.

points.quote: the ratio of one male to three or four females seems to work well
a footprint of approximately 48 inches (120 cm) in length and 18 inches (45 cm) in width
maintain just a single individual alongside 4-6 females
only keeping one male in the breeding tank
100 gallons for a community of four to six peacock cichlids
about 15 fish for a 90-gallon all-male tank

notes: Unit male (harem 1M:3-6F) is consistent across TFH, Seriously Fish and Aquarium Source. No multi-male scaling rule from a good source; Aquarium Source says 100+ gal for a multi-male community. Several quotes are fetch-tool paraphrases; FW 15 males/90 gal is a site reply to a reader. All-male counts of 8-12 in 55-75 gal appear only in forum threads (not used).

rule.text: Practical Fishkeeping: tank of at least 120 cm / 48 in, at least two females per male; Quality Marine mbuna rule about four juveniles per square foot (footprint)

points.quote: a 120cm/48 inch and over mixed mbuna aquarium is best
Keep a group of at least 20 fish.
we recommend keeping several females to each male
about four juvenile fish per square foot
keep the number of yellow lab cichlid males in the tank to a minimum

notes: Quality Marine gives 4 juveniles per sq ft for mbuna generally (75 gal at 4x1.5 ft = about 24; retailer, juveniles). Practical Fishkeeping '20 fish' and 'two females per male' are fetch-tool paraphrases. Labs are the mild mbuna, so counts mostly reflect mixed colonies. No hard 'one male per X' rule found in an article.

points.quote: 250 litres minimum for a group; floor of 12 fish
350 litres or more gives substantially better results; advises 18 to 24
a group of 6-8 young fish
should be overcrowded to reduce aggression and territory formation

notes: Cluster species: aggression falls with MORE fish, so demasoni is a group floor (12) not a cap. Gensou: 12-fish floor at 250 L, 18-24 at 350 L. Seriously Fish 54 gal is its stated absolute minimum. Most quotes are fetch-tool paraphrases. Cichlid-Forum articles were blocked (HTTP 402); forum thread numbers (12 in 55 gal/36 in, 15-20 at 72 in) not used. Existing Aquarium Co-Op 40 gal/5-7 point in expert-curve.

rule.text: Seriously Fish: one per tank; in a very large tank each individual is likely to require a territory with a diameter of at least a metre (the per-fish increment is inferred)

points.quote: each individual is likely to require a territory with a diameter of at least a metre
120cm (48") minimum (keep singularly)
Keeping two red tail sharks together almost always results in the dominant individual persecuting the subordinate
you should only keep one of these per tank as they are extremely territorial

notes: One fish holds a territory; all sources say keep one. The Seriously Fish 1 m territory diameter permits a footprint rule for very large tanks only; no source lists a two-shark tank size.

points.quote: A 55-gallon tank is absolutely minimun--larger will increase the likelihood of success.
a very large tank is required
a harem of one male and at least three females

notes: Seriously Fish 54 gal/120x45 cm is the absolute minimum; one male plus at least 3 females; multiple males only in a very large tank (no size given). SF quotes are fetch-tool paraphrases. Houston Fishbox says 1M + 4-5F (not fetched). No per-male increment found.

points.quote: A breeding group of one male and 3-6 females.
at least 48" in length

notes: Predatory haplochromine, a loner in nature: one male with 3-6 females for breeding at 48 in+; non-breeding, a solitary specimen. 125-200+ gal figures came only from search summaries (not fetched). No multi-male rule.
